critique: The black field and white, softly feathered particle treatment are directionally appropriate, and t4 shows the particles distributing across the frame. However, it still reads as a sparse starfield rather than the preset's enveloping floating-dust field. t1 contains only about five visible particles and t4 only around twenty; the early-frame density remains far below the intended thumbnail look. Size variation is also too extreme: occasional large bright blobs stand out as stars instead of a predominantly fine, diffuse dust population.

suggestions.why: Substantially increase births per frame so the first rendered frame and subsequent frames contain a visibly dense dust field rather than slowly accumulating sparse points.
Reduce the maximum particle size so isolated oversized bright blobs no longer dominate the field and the result reads as fine dust.
Retain organic size variation while reducing the chance of conspicuous star-like particles relative to the dominant small dust grains.
